articles.title: Home Assistant makes room for a whole-home energy meter
articles.dek: A measured household total gets its own place in Energy, instead of appearing again as an appliance.
body: Home Assistant’s Energy dashboard adds a Home source for meters that measure the entire household’s electricity consumption. Owners can supply energy and power readings directly, instead of configuring the whole house as an individual device and duplicating it in the flow diagram.
The change connects the new source to the dashboard’s configuration and energy flow view.

media.caption: The Home source gives a measured household total its own place in the energy flow diagram.

articles.title: Home Assistant’s management AI can call any action
articles.dek: The administrator connection expands beyond dedicated inspection and recovery tools.
body: AI assistants connected to Home Assistant’s system-management interface gain a tool for calling any Home Assistant action. It returns action response data and accepts templates in the target and data, allowing a connected assistant to compose a call and use its result.

This expands the administrator-only management connection beyond the specific log, inspection and integration-reload tools covered earlier this week. That connection is not limited to the household entities exposed to ordinary Assist; the new tool belongs to that broader management scope.
articles.continuity: This extends the inspection tools reported on October 24 and the integration-reload action reported on October 26.

pullRequests.title: Add call action tool to the Home Assistant LLM API
Add Home Assistant LLM API and system log tool

articles.title: Home Assistant builds custom media players from templates
articles.dek: Playback controls and state can be assembled into one player, with a visual setup for common controls.
body: Home Assistant adds media players to its Template integration. Makers can connect existing actions and state readings to a single player with playback, volume, source selection and media information, rather than exposing each operation as a separate control.

Visual setup covers state, power, volume, playback and source selection, with a preview. YAML supports the fuller set of templates and actions, including trigger-based players; saved state and media information return after a restart.

articles.title: Everything Presence sensors gain Works with Home Assistant certification
articles.dek: The Lite, One and Pro join the programme with local control and a commitment to continued support.
body: Everything Smart Home joins Works with Home Assistant with its Everything Presence Lite, One and Pro sensors. In the announcement, Jacqueline Ajayi says all three passed the programme’s tests for local control, privacy and sustainability, with the company committing to long-term support and firmware updates.

The sensors run ESPHome and connect directly to Home Assistant over the home network without a cloud service. All three also act as Bluetooth proxies. Their different hardware suits different rooms: the Lite tracks up to three people across four zones, the One adds temperature and humidity sensing, and the Pro combines two radars with Ethernet and Power over Ethernet for installations using a single cable.

Lewis Barclay, known for the Everything Smart Home video channel, founded the family-run business with his father Dave. The certification covers these three devices; the post says the programme’s testing used a standard Wi-Fi connection.

articles.title: Music Assistant pairs ESPHome speakers through Home Assistant
articles.dek: Compatible devices connect without copying a pairing token between the two systems.
body: Music Assistant uses Home Assistant to pair compatible ESPHome Sendspin devices without asking the owner to paste a pairing token. Its Home Assistant connection follows the devices Home Assistant announces and requests a token when an encrypted, unpaired player connects.

The change connects Music Assistant to the ESPHome pairing support added to Home Assistant earlier this week. Home Assistant fetches the token directly from the device rather than storing it. Both sides need the corresponding support; an older Home Assistant simply leaves automatic pairing off, with manual pairing still available.

Add Sendspin auto pairing support to ESPHome

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps a conversation when an AI request fails
articles.dek: Errors and actions already taken stay in the history, while overlapping messages no longer overwrite each other.
body: Home Assistant keeps a failed message in its conversation history together with the error and any actions the assistant already took. A person can then continue the conversation instead of losing the turn when an AI service stops responding.

A conversation also handles one message at a time. A second message sent before the first finishes receives a busy error instead of competing with it for the same history. Scripts making parallel requests need separate conversation identifiers or must wait for the answer.

articles.title: Home Assistant gives Schlage guest codes an expiry time
articles.dek: Temporary PINs work only between a chosen start and end time.
body: Home Assistant’s Schlage connection adds scheduled access codes for guests or people visiting to carry out work. The add-code action accepts a start and end time, so the code only works during that window without an automation having to delete it afterwards.
Calls without either time continue to create permanent codes. The code-list action also returns each code’s identifier and schedule, making temporary access visible to automations.

articles.title: Home Assistant asks before adding Matter on small hosts
articles.dek: Systems with less than 1.5 GB of memory show the discovery instead of starting Matter Server automatically.
body: Home Assistant OS stops automatically installing and starting Matter Server during onboarding when the host reports less than 1.5 GB of memory. A discovered Matter service is shown for the owner to select instead, with installation progress visible.

The change follows testing on a 1 GB Raspberry Pi 3 where the automatic installation made Home Assistant stop responding. It also covers similarly small virtual machines and other hosts; it does not change the documented 2 GB minimum for Matter Server.

pullRequests.title: Ask before installing the Matter Server during onboarding on hosts with little memory

articles.title: ESPHome updates finished devices without a configuration file
articles.dek: A supplied firmware image and the device’s address are enough for a command-line network update.
body: Owners of finished ESPHome products can send a manufacturer’s firmware image over the network without obtaining or recreating its YAML configuration. The upload command accepts the file and the device’s address directly, removing the need to build a dummy configuration just to pass validation.

The uploader reads the usual update port from the image where possible, or accepts an explicit port. Passwords and encryption keys can be supplied separately. This path sends the existing image without compiling it; serial installation and updates through a device’s web server still need their existing workflows.

pullRequests.title: [core] Allow esphome upload without a configuration

articles.title: Home Assistant controls LibreSync audio hubs locally
articles.dek: The new connection brings source, volume and playback controls to compatible WiSA stereo hubs.
body: Home Assistant adds a local connection for audio hubs built on Libre Wireless’s LibreSync platform. It combines playback state, source selection, volume, transport controls and track information, with automatic discovery or setup by address.
The contributor tested the connection on a Platin Stereo Hub. This first integration covers playback controls; it does not switch the hub’s power or control mute over the network.

articles.title: Home Assistant’s Android app avoids a crash when leaving Wi-Fi
articles.dek: Changing from the home address to the external address keeps the dashboard connection intact.
body: Home Assistant’s Android app fixes a crash when switching from its internal address to the external one, such as when the phone leaves Wi-Fi. The dashboard keeps its existing connection to the app while navigating to the other address.
The contributor reproduced the crash in seven of eight network switches on a Galaxy S25 Ultra and saw none in eight switches with the correction.

articles.title: WattWächter brings gas and water meters into Home Assistant
articles.dek: The connection tracks totals and flow, and handles corrected readings separately from a replaced meter.
body: Home Assistant’s WattWächter connection expands from electricity to the WattWächter Gas and Wasser meter readers. It exposes gas or water volume and flow rates; gas devices also provide a power reading calculated by their firmware.

The counters distinguish correcting a meter reading from replacing the meter, so a downward correction is not mistaken for a new meter’s full consumption. Switching a reader from gas to water or back creates the relevant sensors and removes those for the previous medium.

articles.title: ZHA’s device layer handles battery-free Green Power buttons
articles.dek: EnOcean’s four-button rocker and Philips Hue Tap gain device-specific event handling.
body: ZHA’s device-handling layer adds button events for the EnOcean PTM 216Z four-button rocker and Philips Hue Tap. These battery-free Zigbee Green Power switches send a short message when pressed.

The handlers turn those messages into individual button events and retain the state needed for each button. This completes device-specific handling on top of the pairing and message-processing work in zigpy and ZHA; it is work in those libraries, rather than a new Home Assistant setup screen.

articles.title: Home Assistant controls Homematic’s water shutoff unit
articles.dek: Separate valve, water-alarm and flow readings show what the unit is doing.
body: Home Assistant adds the Homematic IP HmIP-WSS and HmIP-WSS-GB water stop and supply units. Owners can open or close the valve and use the reported water alarm and flow rate in their dashboards and automations.
The alarm and valve remain separate: after a water alarm, the valve stays closed until it is opened again. An alarm clearing therefore does not imply that the water supply has resumed.

articles.title: ESPHome stops leaving Bluetooth devices searching after disconnect
articles.dek: Sleeping devices get time to hear that an ESP32-C3 or ESP32-S3 connection has ended.
body: ESPHome gives sleeping Bluetooth devices more time to hear that an ESP32-C3 or ESP32-S3 connection has ended. Previously, the controller could stop trying too early, leaving the other device searching at full receive power until its own timeout.

In a test using an ESP32-C3 and a thermostat running custom firmware, four of eight disconnects left the thermostat searching for six seconds. None of thirteen did with the correction. That extra search used five to six times the charge of a normal complete connection in this test. A device that has genuinely disappeared takes longer to time out.

pullRequests.title: [esp32_ble] Keep LL_TERMINATE_IND going until acknowledged on ESP32-C3/S3

articles.title: Snapcast announcements finish before the music returns
articles.dek: Music Assistant waits for short messages to play and resumes seekable music where the interruption began.
body: Music Assistant repairs both ends of an announcement on its native Snapcast playback path. Short spoken messages finish playing before the music returns, and seekable music resumes at the position where the announcement interrupted it.

Previously, the music continued unheard during the message, so listeners lost that part of the track. A separate timing problem could cut off the end of a short announcement while audio was still buffered at the speakers. The updated handling waits for that audio before restoring the previous stream and volume.

Radio, live sources and synchronized group members still return to the live stream. The short-message buffer correction applies to native Snapcast handling; external Snapcast servers do not yet supply the buffer information it needs.

Fix Snapcast cutting off the end of short announcements

articles.title: Music Assistant revises its Nest speaker streaming defaults
articles.dek: The earlier blanket Cast change helped the new Google Home Speaker but interrupted older receivers.
body: Music Assistant revises the Cast streaming default covered on October 21 after it interrupted playback on older Nest speakers. A Nest Mini playing Ambient Sounds could stop after five to ten minutes with the setting chosen for the 2026 Google Home Speaker; in the reported test, the earlier setting played overnight.

The default now depends on the receiver. Most Cast devices return to HTTP Profile 3, while the 2026 Google Home Speaker, non-Google Android TV receivers, groups and stereo pairs keep Profile 2. Explicit choices are preserved. Updated troubleshooting guidance says a Cast group and its members should use the same profile.

articles.title: Z-Wave JS corrects passwords sent to compatible locks
articles.dek: Existing passwords written with the old encoding need to be set again.
body: Z-Wave JS corrects passwords sent to locks implementing the User Credential command class. The driver used the wrong text encoding, so a compliant lock could store something different from the password the owner intended.

Passwords written through the earlier implementation need to be set again. PINs and binary credentials are unaffected. A related correction handles non-ASCII user names using the encoding supported by the lock.

fix(cc): encode (Extended) ASCII user names in User Credential CC correctly
